It specifies the cognitive processes and text/task dimensions used to design reading tasks (e.g., locating information, understanding, evaluating and reflecting), and it describes how proficiency is reported via composite scales and subscales/levels. The framework also outlines item difficulty drivers, response formats, and considerations for computer-based delivery and adaptive testing, including how reading fluency can be measured as a descriptive indicator. No empirical model estimation, predictive analytics, or performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) are reported in the provided text, so there are no study-level ML results to interpret for policy beyond the implications of the assessment design choices.
